text.p: Schering-Plough Corp said it expects earnings growth in the "low to mid-teens" in 1997.

In 1996, Schering-Plough said it achieving solid results in its ethical pharmaceutical business, strengthened its research pipeline through internal research and development efforts and new licensing agreements, while maintaining control on expenses.
In the 1996 fourth quarter, the company earned $277.4 million or $0.76 a share on sales of $1.4 billion, up from earnings of $239.4 million or $0.66 a share on $1.3 billion in sales.
Schering-Plough's 1996 results were led by its global pharmaceutical business, which posted 13 percent higher sales.

In the United States, sales of prescription pharmaceuticals were up 23 percent in 1996, driven by growth in all major therapeutic categories: allergy/respiratory, anti-infective/anticancer, dermatological and cardiovascular products, the company said.
